# に vs で — where things happen

**[に (destination)](<../grammar/に.md#destination>)**
:   The goal of movement with 行く・来る・帰る: 学校に行きます。Choose に for where you are headed; an action happening AT a place takes で.

**[に (arrival/entry)](<../grammar/に.md#arrival-entry>)**
:   The place you end up in or at — 着く・入る・住む・座る: ホテルに着いた。The verb lands you there, so it takes に even though it feels like an action.

**[で (action location)](<../grammar/で.md#action-location>)**
:   The stage where an activity happens: 図書館で勉強します。If the verb is something you DO at the place, use で; movement or arrival takes に.

**[では (location)](<../grammar/では.md#location>)**
:   で plus は — how things are within a place or institution: 日本では靴を脱ぎます。For general practice, contrast, and formal statements — for one plain event, で alone usually suffices.
